text.en: Some people can find a fault in sunshine and in rain.

The poem describes a family that lives on Complaining Street in the city of Never-Are-Satisfied, beside the River of Discontent. They growl about everything: the weather is always too hot or too cold, they scold in summer and winter, and nothing ever goes right for them.
The poet uses humour and exaggeration to show how grumbling spoils a happy life. It invites us to mend our ways and be cheerful and thankful.
Learn the word amiss, discontent and growl. Notice the invented place names that make the point, and the rhyming couplets.
